title: The two-word trick for following through
summary: Implementation intentions — 'if X happens, then I'll do Y' — link a goal to a specific moment. A review of 94 studies found they substantially help people act on their goals.
evidenceNote: The meta-analytic evidence is strong, but effect sizes in individual studies vary and some may be inflated by publication bias.

scenes.text: "I'll exercise more" rarely works. Try "if–then" instead.
An implementation intention links a moment to an action: "If it's Monday at 7, then I put on my running shoes."
Turn a wish into a plan.

right.label: If–then plan
right.text: When I get into bed, I'll read one page

scenes.text: A review of 94 studies found if–then plans had a medium-to-large effect on reaching goals.
It works because the decision is made in advance. When the moment arrives, the cue triggers the action.
Pick one goal. Finish this sentence: "When ___, I will ___."

sources.title: Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta-analysis of Effects and Processes
